releases.title: Automatic Pages enablement and push-reset recovery
releases.telegramAnnouncement: The BallerWatch web app deployment now enables GitHub Pages automatically and Web Push recovers cleanly after a factory reset.
changes: Changed the GitHub Pages deployment to self-enable Pages using the existing CRON_GITHUB_PAT when no Pages site has been configured yet, avoiding a manual Settings step when the token has sufficient permission.
Added deployment verification for the live Cloudflare PWA API surface in addition to the existing Telegram webhook/health verification.
Changed PURGE to recreate a fresh empty encrypted VAPID identity immediately after clearing subscriptions and board state so the PWA can be re-enabled without another deployment.
Made the installed PWA detect a rotated VAPID application key, discard its stale browser subscription, and guide the user to enable push again.

releases.title: iPhone web app and Web Push fallback
releases.telegramAnnouncement: BallerWatch now has an installable iPhone web app with a notification board, read-only Q&A, and Web Push fallback when Telegram is unavailable.
changes: Added an installable GitHub Pages PWA at vudh1.github.io/ballerwatch with an iPhone Home Screen experience, offline app shell, dedicated touch icon, notification board, and one-question/one-answer read-only Q&A.

Added standards-based Web Push without a new database or notification provider: VAPID keys and browser subscriptions are generated/managed by GitHub Actions and stored AES-GCM encrypted on runtime-state.
Added Cloudflare Worker endpoints for public-safe web configuration, board reads, read-only Q&A, and encrypted subscribe/unsubscribe registration while keeping state-changing commands on Telegram.

Extended the existing pickup, real RATS schedule-change, and daily version notification allowlist to a Telegram-independent Web Push channel; Telegram delivery failure no longer prevents the public-safe fallback from being recorded and signaled.
Kept Workers KV absent, Cloudflare Cron Triggers disabled, cron-job.org as the 2/5/10-minute scheduler, and the single-parentless runtime-state snapshot model unchanged.
Added privacy regression coverage proving the public web path strips RSVP/waitlist names, owner settings, secrets, and private push material.

releases.title: Automatic GitHub Wiki synchronization
releases.telegramAnnouncement: The repository Wiki now stays synchronized automatically with the canonical docs/wiki documentation.
changes: Made docs/wiki the single source of truth for the GitHub Wiki and removed the separate WIKI_TOKEN dependency.
Changed the Publish wiki workflow to use the repository GITHUB_TOKEN with contents: write and mirror docs/wiki on every relevant main update.
Updated current documentation so Wiki publishing behavior matches the automated workflow.

releases.title: Unified Node.js runtime
releases.telegramAnnouncement: BallerWatch now uses one Node.js runtime for league automation, Calendar reconciliation, tests, and notifications while preserving existing behavior.
changes: Migrated the six remaining league runtime Python modules and their tests to dependency-free Node.js ECMAScript modules.
Removed Python files, Python setup, compilation, unittest discovery, and Python invocations from GitHub Actions.
Preserved existing RATS tracking keys and Calendar fingerprints with Python-compatible canonical hashing plus Pacific DST behavior.
Added Node parity coverage for RATS normalization/retries, Calendar gate/pair/purge/sync, Telegram schedule notifications, and Apps Script in-place event updates.
Kept production architecture, runtime-state encryption, Calendar targeting, cron-job.org scheduling, and Telegram notification policy unchanged.

releases.title: RATS transient-source resilience
releases.telegramAnnouncement: RATS schedule refresh is now more resilient to temporary source outages while preserving verified Calendar state.
changes: Retry only transient RATS source failures with bounded exponential backoff, while permanent authentication/configuration errors fail immediately.
When a valid last-good league schedule already exists, retain it during transient RATS outages instead of failing the production watcher or applying unverified Calendar/Telegram changes.
Added a regression that executes the Apps Script update path and proves an existing tracked Calendar event is updated in place rather than duplicated.
Corrected current purge documentation to reflect that BallerWatch-managed RATS Calendar events are removed while unrelated Calendar events remain untouched.

releases.title: Index-independent Calendar pairing
releases.telegramAnnouncement: Calendar pairing no longer depends on Google Calendar search indexing, so a fresh target marker can be detected immediately.
changes: Changed Calendar target pairing to scan a bounded 21-day event window directly instead of relying on Google Calendar full-text search indexing.
Pairing checks the default Calendar first, then other visible calendars, while preserving the unique-marker proof and private Calendar ID storage.

releases.title: Pair Calendar bridge to intended target
releases.telegramAnnouncement: Calendar sync is now privately paired to the intended Google Calendar instead of relying on the Apps Script owner's default calendar.
changes: Added private Calendar pairing so the Apps Script bridge targets the intended Google Calendar rather than blindly using the deployment owner's default calendar.
Pairing discovers a temporary non-sensitive marker across calendars visible to the Apps Script account, stores only the matched calendar ID in Script Properties, and deletes the marker after pairing.
Before switching targets, the bridge cleans BallerWatch-managed events and stale mappings from the previous target/default calendar to avoid orphaned wrong-calendar events.
Normal Calendar sync now fails closed until a target Calendar has been paired, and no Calendar ID or email is committed or logged.
Moved all unit and smoke test-only code into a dedicated tests/ tree that mirrors source areas, leaving production folders runtime-only.
Condensed README release notes to a short recent-changes section while keeping complete release history in features/versions.json.

releases.title: Stale Calendar mapping cleanup
releases.telegramAnnouncement: Calendar purge now treats mappings to already-deleted events as harmless stale state instead of failing the full reset.
changes: Changed Calendar PURGE so Script Property mappings to events that no longer exist or were already deleted are cleared as stale state rather than treated as fatal errors.
Kept all other Calendar deletion, permission, API, and marker-scan errors fail-closed.
Added stale-mapping counts to purge logs and regression coverage for the reporting path.

releases.title: Calendar purge reliability fix
releases.telegramAnnouncement: Calendar reset is now more resilient and verifies the deployed bridge version before deleting BallerWatch-managed match events.
changes: Hardened Calendar purge so one stale or inaccessible event cannot abort deletion of all other BallerWatch-managed events.
Changed the legacy marker safety scan to bounded yearly Calendar queries and added safe bridge error reporting for operational debugging.
Required the live Apps Script Calendar bridge to report version 3 or newer before a full reset can run.
Added regression coverage for surfaced Calendar purge errors.

releases.title: Full reset and workflow cleanup
releases.telegramAnnouncement: Full reset now clears BallerWatch-managed RATS Calendar events as well as runtime state, and obsolete maintenance workflows were removed.
changes: Expanded PURGE so it deletes only BallerWatch-managed RATS Calendar events through the authenticated Apps Script bridge before clearing runtime-state.
Added a safe Calendar purge action that removes tracked event IDs and marker-tagged legacy BallerWatch events without touching unrelated Calendar events.
Removed the obsolete Configure repository and Seed failover cache workflows; production watchers already maintain failover caches and repository configuration is no longer a recurring operation.
Added Calendar bridge syntax validation and Calendar purge client tests.
Added a one-time release reset hook so this release can deploy the new Calendar bridge, purge Calendar/runtime state, and let the normal 2/5/10-minute production watchers rebuild from scratch.

releases.title: Quiet Telegram notification policy
releases.telegramAnnouncement: Telegram is now quiet by default: only RSVP watcher alerts, direct answers, one combined daily version update, and real league schedule changes are sent.
changes: Restricted proactive Telegram output to RSVP watcher notifications, real league schedule changes, and a single combined version announcement per Pacific day; direct replies to user questions remain unchanged.
Made watchdog failures, watchdog recovery, CI/testing/build activity, unsolicited setup reminders, invalid-setting reminders, and score-only changes silent on Telegram.
Combined every not-yet-announced release into one daily version message using user-facing release summaries instead of commit, pull-request, or other engineering details.
Changed league Calendar fingerprints so score-only changes do not trigger schedule reconciliation or Telegram schedule-update messages.
Removed the standalone Telegram score notifier.

releases.title: Self-healing pickup endpoint
changes: Added a privacy-safe recovery path that rediscovers the current public RSVP Apps Script endpoint when the configured endpoint is missing or retired with HTTP 404/410.
Kept encrypted endpoint overrides and the UPSTREAM_ENDPOINT secret as the primary configuration; discovered endpoint values are never committed, logged, or persisted to runtime state.
Added endpoint extraction/recovery regression tests and verified the live notification-silent pickup smoke succeeds with the stale configured secret.
Extended stale-branch cleanup to remove inactive fix/* branches as well as release/* branches.

releases.title: Runtime-only snapshot tree
changes: Restricted runtime-state root snapshots to the canonical generated runtime paths instead of carrying the repository source tree into the snapshot branch.
Kept the one-parentless-commit retention model and optimistic concurrent-writer protection introduced in 2.5.4.
Expanded runtime-state regression coverage so PURGE produces an empty root tree and a rebuilt snapshot contains only the expected runtime file.

releases.title: Single-snapshot runtime-state retention
changes: Changed runtime-state persistence so each successful write replaces branch history with one parentless snapshot commit containing only the current encrypted runtime files.
Made PURGE compact runtime-state to the same one-commit form while preserving optimistic concurrency with the existing retry behavior.
Added regression coverage proving both a purge and a subsequent state rebuild leave runtime-state with exactly one root commit.
Added automatic cleanup of stale release branches that no longer have an open pull request.

releases.title: Chat-review-driven schedule question fixes
changes: Used privacy-minimized 48-hour chat-review signals to identify recurring failures for today's schedule, specific-date schedules, pickup details, and next/recommended-game wording.
Added deterministic routing and date-aware schedule lookup across both pickup and RATS league data so common read-only questions are answered from existing runtime state before AI.
Expanded bounded Gemini/Groq fallback context with upcoming league matches while keeping private participant data out of prompts.
Added regression tests for the reviewed natural-language phrasings and date-specific fast-path schedule replies.

releases.title: Webhook-only Telegram listener hardening
changes: Removed the GitHub listener's legacy Telegram getUpdates fallback so empty workflow dispatches no-op instead of conflicting with the active Cloudflare webhook.
Processed Cloudflare fast-path history-only dispatches directly before Telegram update handling, fixing failed history persistence runs after the runtime purge.
Made primary cron-job.org scheduler synchronization explicitly disable any legacy Telegram listener polling schedule whenever the management API is available.

releases.title: Optional cron-job.org management API during quota exhaustion
changes: Made the post-merge cron-job.org setup workflow tolerate only temporary management API failures such as HTTP 429/502/503/504 or network timeouts, while authentication errors remain blocking.

Made Telegram Worker deployment independent of temporary cron-job.org management API availability after the Worker, secrets, webhook, health check, and zero-Cloudflare-Cron verification have succeeded.
Kept scheduler correctness fail-closed whenever cron-job.org responds: missing, disabled, duplicated, mistargeted, or wrong-cadence jobs still fail verification.

releases.title: Gemini Flash-first answers and safer runtime recovery
changes: Added Gemini Flash as the preferred bounded natural-language answer provider, with Groq fallback and deterministic/non-AI handling when AI is unavailable or unsuitable.

Preserved the KV-free 2.4 architecture: Cloudflare remains webhook plus read-only fast path, cron-job.org remains the 2/5/10-minute scheduler, and encrypted durable runtime state remains on the runtime-state branch.
Hardened PURGE and clean bootstrap behavior so an available runtime-state branch is authoritative and deleted files cannot be resurrected from legacy Cloudflare or stale Actions-cache backups.
Reduced recurring cron-job.org management API verification to four reads per day while keeping the watchdog itself at 10-minute cadence.

Made temporary cron-job.org management API unavailability such as HTTP 429 non-blocking for release smoke, while authenticated scheduler misconfiguration, missing jobs, disabled jobs, or wrong cadences still fail verification.

Made notification-silent release smoke tolerate only transient RATS source outages when a valid last-good schedule is already present; schema, auth, configuration, and invalid-state failures still block the release.

releases.title: Explicit Cloudflare Cron Trigger removal
changes: Fixed the 2.4.0 cutover so Wrangler explicitly publishes triggers.crons=[]; omitting the property leaves previously deployed Cloudflare Cron Triggers in place.
Added a deployment verification step that reads the Cloudflare Worker schedules API and fails unless the ballerwatch-telegram Worker has zero Cron Triggers after deployment.

releases.title: KV-free runtime and 48-hour chat review
changes: Removed Workers KV and Cloudflare Cron Triggers from the production runtime to eliminate the daily KV request-limit risk; Cloudflare now hosts only the Telegram webhook and read-only fast path with short-lived Cache API use.

Made cron-job.org the primary 2/5/10-minute scheduler and moved durable generated state to a dedicated runtime-state Git branch, with private runtime payloads remaining AES-GCM encrypted and main staying release-oriented.
Added one-time migration from the existing Cloudflare KV runtime into the runtime-state branch before the KV binding is removed, while retaining encrypted GitHub Actions cache as a recovery source.

Replaced automatic feature-request creation for unanswered questions and thumbs-down feedback with a 48-hour Groq-condensed encrypted Telegram history and privacy-minimized bug/feature/negative-feedback review signals.
Kept the Telegram fast path lightweight by persisting condensed history asynchronously to the runtime-state branch after the reply, using the GitHub listener only as a persistence fallback.

releases.title: Cloudflare empty-KV self-bootstrap
changes: Made Cloudflare league refresh recover from empty or freshly purged KV by bootstrapping the built-in monitored-team defaults and rediscovering the current RATS season.
Centralized non-secret default league-team configuration so GitHub and Cloudflare use the same bootstrap values.
Changed GitHub Wiki publishing to wait gracefully for an optional write-capable WIKI_TOKEN instead of failing main when GitHub's normal Actions token cannot initialize the separate wiki repository.

releases.title: Resilient failover and onboarding foundation
changes: Standardized repository code style and module-level documentation, added a dependency-free style checker, expanded CI coverage, and added long-form onboarding/operations documentation under docs/wiki.

Kept all three cron-job.org failover jobs enabled at their 2/5/10-minute cadences while adding a Cloudflare heartbeat gate so pickup and league fallback runs skip duplicate source work when the edge is healthy.
Added encrypted GitHub Actions cache backups of last-known pickup, league, and watchdog runtime state so GitHub fallback can continue when the Worker runtime-state API is unavailable.
Changed PURGE into a full Cloudflare KV runtime factory reset, including custom league-team state; built-in default teams bootstrap again on the next league run.
Added a deterministic intent/tag index before Groq to reduce AI calls and edge latency for common natural-language questions.
Centralized runtime path definitions and persisted the fresh Cloudflare RATS change signal so full league reconciliation can skip a duplicate aggregate API request after edge-triggered changes.
Added a GitHub Wiki publishing workflow and documented architecture, failover, development, operations, release process, and data/privacy boundaries.

releases.title: Release-oriented repo and faster league reconciliation
changes: Cleaned obsolete runtime and scheduler files after the Cloudflare KV migration, including the legacy league status artifact and superseded cron management helpers.

Reduced RATS reconciliation latency by trying the last known valid season first, fetching independent team schedule exports concurrently, and removing unnecessary Node/Python setup steps from the production league workflow.

Added cron-job.org fallback verification: pickup, league and watchdog fallback jobs must exist with their expected 2/5/10-minute cadences, correct workflow targets, and remain disabled while Cloudflare is healthy.
Unified cron-job.org fallback creation, verification, enable and disable behavior in one tested module.
Adopted release branches with notification-silent PR smoke tests and squash-only merges so future main history is one commit per released version.
Serialized release-PR live smoke tests to avoid duplicate upstream traffic and added league watcher timing output for performance regression tracking.

releases.title: KV-only runtime state
changes: Migrated all remaining listener, pickup, league, Calendar, watchdog and feature-request runtime state from tracked repository files into the private Cloudflare KV namespace.
Removed all 12 runtime-state files from GitHub and changed the privacy audit to fail if those runtime paths are ever tracked again.
Updated listener, pickup, league and watchdog workflows to pull state from KV at startup, push updated state back to KV, clean the local runner copy, and never commit runtime data.
Moved manual data purge to Cloudflare KV and updated the notification-silent smoke test to use KV runtime fixtures.
Added protected Worker runtime-state APIs, a public privacy-safe feature-summary endpoint, fast-reply state synchronization, and deployment round-trip verification for all runtime scopes.
Removed the production fallback that read runtime soccer state from GitHub; Cloudflare KV is now the sole runtime-state authority.

releases.title: Cloudflare-first runtime
changes: Cut over recurring pickup, RATS and health checks from cron-job.org/GitHub Actions polling to Cloudflare Cron Triggers with private KV hot state.
Common Telegram read-only questions now stay on the Cloudflare fast path with structured deterministic intent handling, bounded Groq intent classification and short conversation context.

Cloudflare performs lightweight source change detection and dispatches GitHub pickup/league reconciliation only when data changes; GitHub remains responsible for CI, deployment, durable encrypted repository state, Calendar reconciliation and state-changing fallback commands.

Added notification-silent live source verification and KV priming before edge activation, stable webhook authentication, serialized Worker deployments and automatic cron-job.org fallback restoration if an edge deployment fails.
Moved watchdog health semantics from GitHub workflow freshness to Cloudflare KV/source heartbeats and hardened source fingerprints so failed reconciliation dispatches are retried.

releases.title: Cloudflare primary-runtime preview
changes: Added a Cloudflare scheduled edge runtime for 2-minute pickup checks, 5-minute RATS checks, and 10-minute health/deep-watchdog coordination.
Added private Cloudflare KV hot-state support for current soccer snapshots, conversation context, AI budget, fingerprints and scheduler health.
Edge polling dispatches the existing GitHub pickup/league workflows only when source data changes, moving routine GitHub Actions out of the normal polling hot path after cutover.
Added notification-silent shadow refresh verification before legacy cron-job.org schedules are disabled.
Added dynamic KV provisioning with a manual CLOUDFLARE_KV_NAMESPACE_ID fallback, plus Worker bundle and edge-runtime regression tests.
Activation remains gated until Cloudflare KV access is available; failed cutover verification leaves the existing cron-job.org production schedules active.

releases.title: Cloudflare fast path and AI intent routing
changes: Added a Cloudflare read-only fast path that answers common Telegram questions directly from encrypted GitHub state without starting a GitHub Actions runner.
Added short-lived conversation context so follow-up questions such as 'what field?', 'what time?' and 'how many?' can refer to the previously discussed pickup date.
Added Groq intent classification at the edge for natural-language read-only questions while keeping facts and actions deterministic.
Split the free AI budget into 25 edge classifications and 25 GitHub fallback calls per UTC day.
Stored private AI feature-request classification metadata for later improvement without publishing request text.

releases.title: Private feature requests
changes: Replaced public request text, IDs and timestamps with an allowlisted category/count summary; original requests remain encrypted.
Added request privacy regression tests, strict public-summary schema validation and a listener audit before state commits.
Preserved encrypted request archives on decryption failure and documented dedicated-key migration requirements.

releases.title: Direct-main maintenance and silent testing
changes: Allowed validated repository maintenance changes to commit directly to main again and removed the PR-only governance requirement.
Made the manual smoke test notification-silent: it verifies refreshed pickup and league data without sending Telegram messages or changing Google Calendar.
Removed default monitored team names from README while keeping the configured defaults in code.
Updated scheduled ChatGPT maintenance guidance to sync current repository instructions before changes and avoid Telegram notifications during testing.

releases.title: Manual data purge and protected main
changes: Added a manual Purge current data GitHub Action that clears generated pickup, league, Calendar-reconciliation, watchdog, and feature-request data while preserving configuration and secrets.
Added repository governance setup for a concise GitHub description and PR-only normal changes to main, with a narrow GitHub Actions bypass for encrypted runtime-state persistence.
Simplified README and agent guidance and required scheduled ChatGPT maintenance to sync from current main and use branch + pull request changes.

releases.title: Deleted Calendar event recovery
changes: Versioned league Calendar tracking keys so stale Apps Script event-ID mappings from manually deleted Calendar events are invalidated.
The Calendar bridge now falls back to matching an active event or creating a fresh event instead of reusing the previous tracking property.
Added regression coverage for the versioned Calendar tracking key.

releases.title: Concurrent state replay hardening
changes: Reworked workflow state persistence to replay generated encrypted state onto the latest main branch before each push attempt.
Prevents rebase conflicts from losing Calendar-applied league snapshots when listener, pickup, league, or watchdog workflows commit concurrently.

releases.title: Default league team bootstrap
changes: Added Third Touch FC and PhoSaiGon as built-in league defaults in that priority order for clean/fresh state.
Encrypted Telegram-managed league team state remains authoritative after bootstrap, so teams can still be added, removed, or renamed.
Purged previously retrieved pickup and league match snapshots before clean-bootstrap end-to-end testing.

releases.title: Calendar bridge deployment compatibility
changes: Updated the Apps Script deployment workflow to replace the Code.js filename produced by clasp pull, avoiding duplicate Code.js/Code.gs conflicts.
Verified the full Calendar bridge CI path: project pull, code push, existing deployment update, live webhook health check, and OAuth cleanup.

releases.title: One-time release announcements
changes: Replaced the single last-announcement marker with persisted announcement-ID history so each enabled release/feature announcement is delivered only once per stored bot state.
Historical announcements are marked seen during migration so older releases cannot rotate back into Telegram.
Cleared all currently stored public/redacted and encrypted/private feature suggestions.

releases.title: Concurrent state persistence hardening
changes: Added bounded pull/rebase/push retries to listener, pickup, league, and watchdog state persistence.
Prevents transient Git ref races between independently scheduled workflows from dropping otherwise successful runs.

releases.title: League team migration reliability
changes: Fixed legacy league-team migration so a valid legacy configuration replaces an existing empty encrypted placeholder.
Preserved the rule that only encrypted league-team state is persisted in BallerWatch.

releases.title: Operational setup runbooks
changes: Added an agent skill for safely discovering and verifying the pickup UPSTREAM_ENDPOINT without committing its live value.
Added repository agent guidance so future maintenance uses the endpoint-discovery procedure and preserves privacy.
Clarified that TRACKER_STATE_KEY is optional when the existing deployment uses the TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN encryption fallback.
Expanded the validation workflow triggers so version history and operational guidance changes are validated automatically.

releases.title: Versioned release history
changes: Added a SemVer release ledger with current version and chronological change history.
Telegram feature announcements now include the release version.
Added /version and version commands to report the current release and latest changes.
Scheduled ChatGPT maintenance tasks must record a release entry whenever they change the product.

releases.title: Automated infrastructure provisioning
changes: Added idempotent cron-job.org API provisioning for listener, pickup, league, and watchdog workflows.
Added automated Google Apps Script Calendar bridge deployment using the existing deployment ID.
Hardened privacy checks against committing Apps Script OAuth/config credentials.

releases.title: BallerWatch consolidated baseline
changes: Consolidated pickup, league, Telegram, Calendar, watchdog, privacy, and feature-builder automation into BallerWatch.
Kept live soccer data and user configuration encrypted at rest.
Added watchdog recovery, manual smoke testing, and privacy-redacted feature requests.
